scenes.text: In 1899, a man walked into the United States Patent Office holding a tiny piece of bent wire.
scenes.image: a man in a 1890s suit and bowler hat entering a grand Victorian patent office lobby, holding up a small paperclip, sunlight through tall windows

scenes.text: Today, Americans buy billions of them every year. They sit on almost every desk in the country.
scenes.image: a huge pile of shiny paperclips spilling across a wooden office desk, warm lamp light

scenes.text: But here's the twist. The man with the patent never invented the paperclip at all.
scenes.image: close-up of a surprised 1890s clerk holding a magnifying glass over an old patent drawing, dramatic shadows
